currentState: How many: 40 events, all published, 0 drafts, across 11 eras (apostolic 4, persecution 6, imperial-conciliar 6, christological 5, iconoclasm 4, byzantine-expansion 3, estrangement 2, late-byzantine 3, ottoman 2, global-missions 1, modern 4). Importance 1: 24, importance 2: 15, importance 3: 1. Seven carry an On This Day calendar date (foundation-of-constantinople, great-schism-1054, sack-1204, fall-1453, alaska-mission, oca-autocephaly, moscow-constantinople-schism-2018).

How thin: body prose (context, narrative, chronology, significance, consequences) totals 14,278 words; median about 240 words per event. 32 of 40 sit between 192 and 267 words: one context paragraph, one or two narrative paragraphs, one significance paragraph. Five sit at 348 to 433 (edict-of-milan, great-schism-1054, fall-of-constantinople, first-council-of-nicaea, pentecost). Only three are long: council-of-florence 2,239 (the only one with a chronology), moscow-constantinople-schism-2018 1,362, ukrainian-autocephaly 1,327.

Sources: 28 of 40 cite exactly 3; 16 events have no source with a link at all (pentecost, council-of-jerusalem, great-schism-1054, fall-of-constantinople, hesychast-councils, alaska-mission, bolshevik-persecution and others). Much of the secondary set is in-copyright scholarship (Tanner, Davis, Kelly, McGuckin, Bruce): fine to cite, never to quote. 19 have an uncertainty note, 8 have consequences.

People: there is no people section. 31 events link saints through rel.saints, shown only as blue links in the Related foot; 9 have none (non-chalcedonian-estrangement, second-iconoclasm, triumph-of-orthodoxy, sack-1204, fall-1453, moscow-patriarchate, oca-autocephaly, ukrainian-autocephaly, 2018 schism). Scripture refs (rel.scripture) render as plain text, not links into the Bible.

Pictures: 9 of 40 events have media (16 JPEGs, 4.3 MB in public/history/media, bundled in the native export because public/ ships wholesale). They are shown ONLY to Plus readers with Immersive on (EventHero, cinematic EventCard). A free reader sees no picture anywhere in History.

The red dot is in four places: EventCard marker bg-crimson on every importance-1 event (24 of 40), EraHeader bg-crimson dot beside each era's years (11), ContinueExploring's bg-crimson dot, and the crimson thumb border while dragging the scrubber (.history-scrubber:active) and TimelineFastScroll.

The colored era backgrounds are Immersive's .cinema-era::before radial gradients tinted by ERA_HUE (11 hues, on by default for entitled readers, so the owner sees them), plus the page-sized .account-atmosphere and the hue-tinted drop cap and ornaments on event pages.

Era headers are not sticky (the EraHeader comment claims they are). The only sticky thing is the control row (.history-controls, top 72px web, 0 native, bg-night/95 with backdrop-blur-sm in the scroll path). On native, NativeBackBar is also sticky top-0 (z-30, backdrop blur), so the control row likely slides under it when stuck; not verified on a phone.

Banned forms still present: unicode ornaments including sparkle stars (EventArticle ERA_ORNAMENT), literal → and ← glyphs (EventCard, ViewInHistory, EventRelations, and in catalog strings study.history.openFullAccountArrow, viewInHistoryArrow, exploreTimelineArrow, study.exploreTheInteractiveTimeline, study.earlier), DM Serif Display where it actually renders (CenturyScrubber output, TimelineFastScroll bubble, .account-dropcap), gold (Immersive toggle on-state border-gold/bg-gold/text-gold, OnThisDayHistory text-gold/80), a blockquote side stripe (border-l-2), tinted boxes (uncertainty aside, ImmersivePreviewCard, EventChip bg-paper/[0.03]), a custom LockMark svg instead of the Plus mark.

A century range input sits in the page flow and a second vertical rail (fast scroll) appears on the right edge. Category chips and a certainty label sit on every card.

buildSteps.step: 3. The line: one quiet vertical line, drawn node, sticky era headers
buildSteps.detail: Line: a single 1px paper/12 border on the list, nodes on it. TimelineNode is an SVG in currentColor with a night-filled knockout so the line never crosses it: 'event' a 9px hollow ring (stroke 1.5, paper/45), 'major' (importance 1) the ring with a 3px center in paper/80, 'current' (the scroll spy's active row, or the selected row on lg+) filled paper/90; the fill change is a 200ms color transition under motion-safe: (data-motion only). Rows: no card box, no category chips, no certainty label; date and region (caption, paper/60), title (h3, Lora title-sm), preview (DM Sans detail, paper/65, 2-line clamp); whole row is the tap target, min 64px. Era header: sticky, one line, solid bg-night (no backdrop blur, Android scroll), hairline bottom, label in Lora, years tabular, a drawn ChevronDown; tapping opens the Eras sheet; the blurb (DM Sans, not italic serif) scrolls under it. Sticky top comes from one CSS variable (--history-sticky-top) set for MobileTopBar height on phones (3rem plus the safe inset) and the AppNav height on md+ web. Controls: on phones the search and filter move into MobileTopBar's trailing slot (Search and Sliders icons from components/ui/icons; the filter count as text, never a dot); the in-flow control row and the in-flow century range go; the century slider moves into the Eras sheet under the era list; TimelineFastScroll is removed below lg (one line only). Add /history and /history/[slug] to OWN_HEADER_PATTERNS so native shows one bar, not the NativeBackBar too. Landing: left-aligned lead (h1, Lora), the count as one plural key, Continue as a quiet row with a chevron, no dot. Scroll: replace the hard-coded 120px reference line and scroll-mt-36 with the sticky stack height so restore and jumps land under the sticky header; set .history-cv contain-intrinsic-size to the measured row height (it is 132px for today's cards; rows will be shorter), measured at 360, 390, 768 as the .cv-card note did. Empty state: plain text plus a Clear filters button, no box. lg+ keeps the context rail and xl the research column, with the same line, nodes and headers. Skeleton: the line and row placeholders.

buildSteps.step: 5. The event page in four parts
buildSteps.detail: Phone frame: MobileTopBar (back, 'Orthodox History', trailing Bookmark, Share, and Listen once history audio exists); the slim bar shows the event's shortTitle after the header scrolls away. Then EventPlate (free, one picture), the header (era short label, date and region as a caption, h1 Lora, the summary as a DM Sans lede), a row of four pills that jump to the parts (anchor links, the current part filled by an IntersectionObserver), then the parts as Lora h2: What happened (context paragraphs first, then narrative, then Step by step only when chronology exists, as a plain dated list without dots or rule); Why it matters (significance, then consequences under a small 'What flowed from it' subhead); The people (EventPeople rows: the saint's own icon thumbnail from lib/saints when a saint slug exists, name linking to /saints/<slug>, a one-line role; people without a saint page get name and role only, no picture); Sources ('How sure we are': CertaintyBadge with its gloss plus the uncertainty note as plain text, then Primary sources, Further reading, and 'In Scripture' with each ref linked to /bible/<book>/<chapter>#v<verse> through lib/search/references referencesIn). Our prose in DM Sans; blockquote blocks (verbatim Scripture, Fathers, councils) in Lora italic with the citation line. Related foot: What led here and What flowed from it as rows with chevrons, related councils/theology/heresies with catalog group titles, Earlier and Later neighbors with drawn chevrons. Non-English locales: ContentNotYetTranslated kind='history' at the top (keys exist). Plus: one row with the Plus mark ('Immersive History') that opens the upgrade sheet; for entitled readers it shows the gallery under the plate (EventHero slimmed to the gallery and a slow pan under motion-safe:, no atmosphere, no parallax if it costs frames). Server-rendered HTML for every part stays crawlable; add og:image from the plate on the web.
i18nKeys: study.history.immersiveRow (Immersive History, more pictures and slow motion)

buildSteps.step: 6. Pictures from the web, not the bundle
buildSteps.detail: webAsset(path): the relative path on the website; SITE_URL + path in a native build (lib/platform/buildTarget.ts at build time for server components, so the static HTML already holds the absolute URL and nothing mismatches on hydration). purifyapp.net already answers picture files with Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin (next.config.ts PICTURE_SOURCES), so https://localhost and capacitor://localhost can draw them; prove it with a cross-origin browser probe, not curl (a 200 is not a picture shown). Append ['public','history','media'] at the END of STASH_PATHS (slot-index rule) so the folder leaves the export: about 4.3 MB off the bundle that sits at 84.4 of 85 MB packed. Media schema: hero path may be .webp, add shape ('wide' | 'portrait') and focus (object-position) for the crop; one picture per event is the rule, gallery stays optional and Plus. fetch-history-media.mjs: copy fetch-section-media.mjs's Commons extmetadata gate (public domain family only, reject NC/ND), write 1200px WebP around 80 to 140 KB, print the registry literal and append HISTORY_MEDIA.md (file, event, work, artist, date, licence, Commons link, and a Rejected table like SECTION_MEDIA.md). Every picture is opened and looked at before it is committed (rules: never ship an image unseen, picture crops). Re-encode the existing 16 JPEGs to WebP only if it saves real bytes on the web; they no longer touch the bundle either way.

buildSteps.step: 7. Data shape for the structure, and the review marker
buildSteps.detail: Keep the existing body keys (the content package merges bodies as they are, scripts/build-content-package.mjs) and add: people: {name: string; saint?: string; role: string}[] (ordered), and review: {status: 'awaiting-clergy-review'; drafted: 'YYYY-MM-DD'; basis: string} (data only, not shown to readers unless he says so). Registry: depth: 'full' | 'short' to mark the rewritten events. Integrity for depth 'full': people length >= 2 and every saint slug resolves; narrative plus context >= 450 words; significance present; at least 2 primary sources and at least 1 with an https link to a public-domain text (CCEL, NewAdvent NPNF/ANF, archive.org scans); media present with shape; review.status set. Every event, full or short, keeps the current gates. Moving labels out of events.ts: era, category and certainty arrays keep ids only; components read t('study.history.era.<id>.label') etc.; HistorySearch keeps English aliases for matching.

The proposed 20 (open question 5, his yes or swaps), chronological, every era covered at least once, 19 of them already marked importance 1: Pentecost; Council of Jerusalem; the Great Persecution; St Anthony and the desert; Edict of Milan; Nicaea I (325); Constantinople I (381); Ephesus (431); Chalcedon (451); Nicaea II (787); Triumph of Orthodoxy (843); Cyril and Methodius; the baptism of Rus (988); 1054; 1204; the hesychast councils (1341 to 1351); the fall of Constantinople (1453); the Philokalia (1782, the Ottoman era's only spiritual landmark in the set); the Alaska mission (1794); the Bolshevik persecution and the new martyrs (from 1917). Four of them (1054, 1204, 1453, Alaska) are On This Day dates, so Today's card lands on a full piece. Left for wave 2: Paul's missions, Nero and the martyrdom of Peter and Paul, the founding of Constantinople, first iconoclasm (folded into Nicaea II's context), and the three long ones restructured into the four parts (Florence, Ukraine 2018, Moscow and Constantinople 2018), then the remaining 15 short ones. Order: Nicaea first (the longform paper in purify-ads/longform/01-constantine/week1.md section 3 is its draft; the video and the app must match), then chronological. Per event: What happened 500 to 900 words, Why it matters 150 to 300, The people 3 to 8, at least 2 primary sources. Canon rules: verbatim quotes only from public-domain translations, cited (Acts and the Epistles from the app's public-domain Bible; Eusebius, Socrates, Athanasius' Life of Antony, Lactantius, the conciliar creeds, definitions and canons from Percival's NPNF 2nd series vol. 14 rather than Tanner, which is in copyright; John of Damascus on the images, Allies 1898). Where the only English translation is in copyright (Choniates, Palamas' Triads, the Russian Primary Chronicle in its common editions, the Philokalia in English), paraphrase in our own words with the citation, never quote. Contested matters (1054 and its dating, Ephesus and Chalcedon and the non-Chalcedonians, Rus as shared heritage, the Bolshevik years) state each side's usage plainly, set certainty honestly, and keep the tone of the Church's own feasts. Every text gets review.status 'awaiting-clergy-review'. Picture candidates to fetch, read the licence on Commons, and open before shipping: keep the existing five (Pentecost Novgorod icon, Nicaea, Triumph of Orthodoxy icon, 1204, 1453); new: the Synaxis of the Twelve Apostles icon (Jerusalem), St Anthony's existing saint icon (no download), Sts Constantine and Helen icon (Milan), the Paris gr. 510 Homilies of Gregory miniature of the council of 381, a Third Council icon or Menologion miniature (Ephesus), Surikov's Fourth Ecumenical Council of 1876 (Chalcedon), a Seventh Council Menologion miniature or icon (Nicaea II), an icon of Sts Cyril and Methodius, Vasnetsov's Baptism of Prince Vladimir (Rus), the Madrid Skylitzes miniature of Patriarch Michael Keroularios (1054), an icon of St Gregory Palamas (hesychasm), the 1782 Venice Philokalia title page (Philokalia), a period view of the Kodiak settlement (Alaska; modern icons of St Herman are in copyright), a period photograph of St Tikhon (1917). Watch for watermarked Vatican scans and minaret-dominated Hagia Sophia frames (both already rejected once in SECTION_MEDIA.md).

Add every new key in all 21 catalogs (the agent translates, no paid API), drop the fragment keys study.eventsAcross and study.erasCouncilsAndSchismsSaints once the plural count key replaces them, no em dashes anywhere. calmHistory.test.ts reads components/history and app/(app)/history as text and fails on bg-crimson, border-crimson, font-display-serif, gold tokens, era-hue, cinema-era, the ornament glyphs and arrow characters, and on any '/history/media/' string not passed through webAsset. Then run Impeccable's check plus a look by eye at 360, 390, 768, 1024 and 1366 in light and dark palettes before he sees anything.

Update the smoke spec (see testsAffected). npm run typecheck (delete *.tsbuildinfo first), npm run test:unit, npm run build:android then npm run build:ios one after the other (export-size should fall by about 4.3 MB), a cross-origin probe that a history picture draws from https://localhost, the phone walk on Android and iPhone: sticky headers under the one top bar, the node lighting while scrolling, the peek sheet dragging, Back from an event returning to the same row, offline open of an event (plate collapses, text stays), RTL (Arabic, Urdu) chevrons mirrored. No push, no CI run without his word.

The clergy-review marker: keep it in the data only (recommended), or show readers a quiet line such as 'Awaiting review by Orthodox clergy' on each piece. Also still open from the notes: does anyone besides a future priest review the history text.
risks: Offline: the apps are local-first and today's pictures are bundled. Loaded from the web, a reader with no signal sees no picture; the plate must collapse cleanly and the text must stand alone. First view costs data on cellular.

Bundle: removing public/history/media saves about 4.3 MB, the biggest single win available against the 85 MB packed ceiling (84.4 now). Adding the new pictures to public/history/media without the stash entry would push the export over the ceiling; the stash test guards it. STASH_PATHS must be appended at the end (killed builds recover by slot index).

Cross-origin pictures: a 200 from curl does not prove the app can draw it; the CORP cross-origin rule covers .jpg/.webp today, but a probe from another origin in a real browser is required before claiming it works on phones.

Sticky stack and scroll restore: the 120px reference line, scroll-mt-36 and contain-intrinsic-size 132px are tuned to today's cards and headers; sticky era headers under a 3rem plus safe-inset top bar change every number, and a wrong placeholder height repeats the saints-list bug (a reader returned seven screens from where they were).

Android scroll performance: no backdrop blur on any sticky bar in the scroll path (the control row and NativeBackBar use it today), and sticky headers must not fight content-visibility on rows; measure on the mid-range Android phone, not the PC.

Content rights: much of the existing citation set is in-copyright scholarship and several standard translations are too (Tanner, Choniates, Palamas' Triads, the Russian Primary Chronicle in common editions, the English Philokalia). Quote only from public-domain translations; anything else is paraphrased with its citation. Never invent a patristic line.

Sensitive history: 1054, the non-Chalcedonian estrangement, the baptism of Rus (Kyiv and Moscow both claim it), the Bolshevik persecution, and the two modern autocephaly pieces need each side's usage stated plainly and certainty set honestly; no priest is reviewing now, so every text ships marked for a future clergy review.

Picture subjects: a valid licence has produced wrong pictures before (a wiring diagram, a mosque-looking Hagia Sophia, a watermarked Vatican scan, a crop that cut a face); modern icons of recent saints (St Herman, the new martyrs) are usually in copyright, so those events need period photographs or engravings instead.
Plus regression: making one picture free shrinks the Immersive layer; if the wording in plans.ts is not changed with it, the paywall describes a feature that partly became free.

i18n: moving 87 era, category and certainty strings plus the new part and plural keys into 21 catalogs is large; the count line must use one plural key, since the current concatenated fragments read wrong in most languages. Event content stays English, so non-English readers see the not-yet-translated notice on every event page until the content is translated.
Smoke tests and their flake history: the expand-card helper exists because of a 60s hydration flake on CI #318; the new peek-sheet path needs the same 'retry until state sticks' care.
